#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR fixes flake reported in #126400

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #126400, #125466

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
- This PR introduces a shared lock over a static port range. This range is shared between two tests, and it reserves a port before allocating it.
- The PR has been tested against a setup using kind + cloud-provider-kind load balancer.
- A parallel run of `should handle updates to ExternalTrafficPolicy field` and `should release NodePorts on delete` on the same node has not been performed as part of the local test.
- With the current approach, only the first available free port is returned, which would essentially lead to higher ports being used less frequently or never. A random allocation approach was considered but was discarded due to the non-deterministic nature of random functions and the potential to never reach a free random port if only a few are available.

Thanks for your reply. Okay makes sense, then I will post a PR with functionality
-  to `Reserve` and `Unreserve` nodeports. and
-  In case any  service is created/updated and assigned a `reserved`  nodeport, it will be deleted and creation/updation will be retried n times  till it gets a nodeport that is not reserved.

>  with a big comment saying new tests should not use THAT functionality

Do we specifically want to avoid using `Reserve` and `Unreserve` nodeports functions in new tests ? My assumption was that these functions could be useful even in new tests, especially in scenarios where a nodeport is de-allocated and reachability is tested. In such cases, the expected failure of reachability can only be guaranteed if the nodeport isn't allocated to another service.

> I don't think you want to do it this way (calling into a method that creates the service). Particularly given that in one case you're reserving a NodePort an in another case a HealthCheckNodePort.

I was trying to avoid more consumption of these methods, your approach sounds simpler though

Thanks for pointing out the article. Considering only static ports for these two tests would greatly simplify the implementation. I am also considering 
- to combine `e2eservice.GetUnusedStaticNodePort()` and `e2eservice.ReserveStaticNodePort(port)` in order to avoid race between two calls
- moving looping part inside `GetUnusedStaticNodePort()` so that a call to this would return a free port

I will post a PR soon and we can address these implementation details there.
